clue.text: Finds tatty brass monkey with it, but not due to continual effort!

indicators.note: to monkey with something is to tamper with it, so these three words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone tampers with shoddy brass fittings, and the result owes nothing to steady work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'monkey with it' rearranges FINDS TATTY BRASS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Progress made in irregular bursts rather than through sustained labour is made in spurts.

clue.text: Bad definition to describe something so!

definitions.text: Bad definition to describe something so!

parts.words: Bad definition to describe something so!
parts.note: definition here is the sharpness of an image, as on a screen or photograph, and poor sharpness gives a smudged picture

explanation.surface: A lexicographer complains about a poorly worded dictionary entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An image with poor definition, in the photographic sense, looks fuzzy and indistinct.

clue.text: In Scotland, a Pole played these pipes

parts.note: Fife is a region of eastern Scotland
S stands for the South Pole

explanation.surface: A Polish musician in Scotland plays the bagpipes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a Pole' looks like a Polish person; it is one of the Earth's poles, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: Small high-pitched flutes used in military bands are wind instruments, loosely pipes.

clue.text: Bride up in arms, and groom cross over it!

definitions.text: Bride up in arms, and groom cross over it!

parts.words: Bride up in arms, and groom cross over it!
parts.note: by tradition a groom carries his bride in his arms over the doorstep of their new home

explanation.surface: An angry bride and her groom quarrel at the wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up in arms' suggests anger and 'cross' suggests annoyance; both are literal: she is lifted, and they pass over something.
explanation.definitionFit: The doorway sill of a house is what a newly married couple traditionally crosses together.

clue.text: At Christmas, sings its head off and attacks

indicators.note: the first letter of the carolling word is removed

parts.note: to wassail is to go carol singing at Christmas

explanation.surface: A carol singer belts out songs at Christmas while assaulting people.
explanation.definitionFit: To set upon someone violently or with criticism is to assault or attack them.

clue.text: Sounds rather like plaintive calls for such redress!

definitions.text: Sounds rather like plaintive calls for such redress!

parts.words: Sounds rather like plaintive calls for such redress!
parts.note: plaintive sounds rather like plaintiff, and a plaintiff in court calls for money as compensation

explanation.surface: Mournful cries for justice are heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Money awarded by a court to compensate for loss or injury is the legal redress sought.

clue.text: Holy man set up checks

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A holy man devises examinations.
explanation.definitionFit: Examinations or trials used to verify something are checks.

clue.text: Doesn't fancy being like this

parts.note: fancy here means imagine or indulge in flights of fancy, not desire

explanation.surface: Someone is reluctant to be a certain way.
explanation.definitionFit: A practical person grounded in facts avoids fantasy and sees things as they are.

clue.text: Got from Labour wet!

definitions.meaning: ... labour is work exploited from underpaid workers, so goods made that way are ...

explanation.definitionFit: Exploited, underpaid toil is called sweated labour; perspiring leaves one damp.

clue.text: Sets a standard for the military, perhaps?

definitions.text: Sets a standard for the military, perhaps?

parts.words: Sets a standard for the military, perhaps?
parts.note: a standard is a regimental flag, and setting one flying means spreading it open

explanation.surface: Someone lays down a benchmark for the armed forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard' looks like a level of quality; it is a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: Opening out a rolled flag so it can fly is spreading it open.

clue.text: A muscle relaxant got from rubber!

definitions.text: A muscle relaxant got from rubber!

parts.words: A muscle relaxant got from rubber!
parts.note: the rubber is a person who rubs, a masseur, not the material

explanation.surface: A drug that relaxes muscles is extracted from latex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubber' looks like the material from trees; it is someone who rubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Kneading the body eases tense muscles, the treatment a masseur gives.

clue.text: Being in opposition, is inside taking a nap

indicators.note: the little word is placed within the word for napping

parts.note: resting means taking a nap
taken as written

explanation.surface: A protester is caught dozing.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposing or standing against something is withstanding it.

clue.text: The quick and the dead, Dean!

definitions.meaning: quick in the sense of fast
Jonathan ..., Dean of St Patrick's in Dublin and author of Gulliver's Travels, is long dead

explanation.definitionFit: Fast means rapid; the long-dead satirist Jonathan was Dean of St Patrick's Cathedral, Dublin.

clue.text: May be said of all powerful rulers

definitions.text: May be said of all powerful rulers

parts.words: May be said of all powerful rulers
parts.note: all powerful read as all-powerful describes absolute rulers, tyrants

explanation.surface: A remark applies to every mighty monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyrants with absolute authority are all-powerful rulers.

clue.text: Moving from a very cold environment

definitions.text: Moving from a very cold environment

parts.words: Moving from a very cold environment
parts.note: the movement is trembling caused by intense cold, not relocation

explanation.surface: Someone relocates away from a freezing place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving from' suggests leaving; it is shaking because of the cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Trembling with cold is the involuntary shaking a freezing place causes.

clue.text: Able to see and be seen

explanation.definitionFit: Having vision means not blind; being spotted means being observed.

clue.text: Gunner reigned over one of the guards

indicators.note: over suggests something knocked over and reformed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, whose soldiers are gunners

explanation.surface: An artilleryman ruled over a guardsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' rearranges RA plus REIGNED. The Grenadier Guards are a British Army regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier of the Grenadier Guards regiment of the British Army is a guardsman.

clue.text: Wildness out of order when bearing away cheat

indicators.note: the letters of the first word are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: S, south, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Unruly behaviour, carried off, cheats people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' takes a compass bearing S out of WILDNESS, and 'out of order' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: To defraud someone is to swindle or cheat them.

clue.text: Wrongly presume it means the greatest

indicators.note: the letters of the next word are wrongly ordered and must be put right

explanation.surface: It is a mistake to assume something is the best.
explanation.definitionFit: Highest in rank or quality is the greatest.

clue.text: Noble dominion for him

parts.note: the territory or rank held by a nobleman of the third rank

explanation.surface: A lord's realm is described.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank or estates of a count-equivalent British nobleman form his domain.

clue.text: Cut in the typing. pool needed, office work being duplicated

definitions.text: Cut in the typing. pool needed, office work being duplicated

parts.words: Cut in the typing. pool needed, office work being duplicated
parts.note: a wax sheet was cut by typing on it, then used to run off copies on a duplicating machine

explanation.surface: Typists are needed to copy office documents.
explanation.walkthrough: Before photocopiers, office copies were made by typing onto a waxed sheet and running it through a duplicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A waxed sheet cut by typewriter keys was used to print multiple copies in old offices.

clue.text: Head for the Big Top? Quite the reverse

definitions.text: Head for the Big Top? Quite the reverse

parts.words: Head for the Big Top? Quite the reverse
parts.note: reversed, the phrase becomes a big top for the head: a large hat

explanation.surface: Someone sets off for the circus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big Top' suggests a circus tent; the reverse is a big top worn on the head, a tall cowboy hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-brimmed, high-crowned cowboy hat is a large covering worn on the head.

clue.text: They ruin hose used by firemen

explanation.definitionFit: Runs in stockings spoil hosiery; climbing frames with rungs are carried by fire crews.

clue.text: Slyly looks for equals

definitions.meaning: to peer is to look narrowly or furtively

explanation.definitionFit: Peeping furtively is looking narrowly; one's equals in rank are those of the same standing.

clue.text: Stone pitcher may have one!

parts.note: pitcher is someone who throws stones, not a jug made of stone

explanation.surface: An earthenware jug might come with something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone pitcher' looks like a stoneware jug; it is a person who hurls stones, like David with Goliath.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap for hurling stones, as David used against Goliath, is a throwing weapon.

clue.text: So to speak, took part in a crime already committed

definitions.text: So to speak, took part in a crime already committed

parts.words: So to speak, took part in a crime already committed
parts.note: people taking part in a police reconstruction act out a crime again

explanation.surface: Someone was an accessory to a past offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting out a past event again, as in a police reconstruction, is performing it once more.

clue.text: He painted out one man of great stature

indicators.note: the letter for one is taken out of the painter's name

parts.note: Titian was a Venetian Renaissance painter
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A painter is said to have depicted a towering figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A giant of mythology, now any person of great importance or size.

clue.text: Being spiritually uplifted, died-fie, what nonsense!

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are nonsense until rearranged

explanation.surface: A worshipper exclaims at the idea of death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what nonsense' rearranges DIEDFIE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Instructed and improved morally or spiritually is the sense of this word.

clue.text: Knocked down in an alley

parts.note: the alley is a bowling alley where pins are toppled, not a back street

explanation.surface: Someone is mugged in a back street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alley' suggests a mugging; it is a bowling alley.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin felled by the ball in ninepins is the bowling target.

clue.text: They're on hand to make announcement of betrothal

definitions.text: They're on hand to make announcement of betrothal

parts.words: They're on hand to make announcement of betrothal
parts.note: on hand literally means worn on the finger, signalling a couple plan to marry

explanation.surface: Staff stand by to announce a couple's engagement.
explanation.definitionFit: Bands given when a couple agree to marry are worn on the finger.
